claim: Voucherify positions itself as an 'Incentive Optimization Engine' for enterprises with modules for incentive decisioning, orchestration, analytics, promotion engine, loyalty, referrals, gift cards/store credit, bundling, digital wallets, and gamification; target buyers are enterprise marketing and loyalty teams in QSR, fintech, retail/ecommerce, travel.
page_title: Incentive Optimization Engine for Enterprises | Voucherify
notes: Homepage self-description; module list corroborated by docs structure.

claim: Voucherify claims API-first architecture with hundreds of endpoints, SDKs in JavaScript, Python, PHP, Java, Ruby, .NET, sub-50ms real-time decisioning responses, 99.99% uptime SLA, ISO 27001 certification, GDPR compliance, auto-scaling for millions of requests, and clients including Trainline, CarParts, Breville, KFC, Vodafone, Michelin, easyJet.
page_title: Incentive Optimization Engine for Enterprises | Voucherify
notes: Latency and uptime figures are marketing claims; uptime corroborated by status page (VOUCHERIFY-023).

claim: Public developer documentation covers a full API surface: validation rules, qualifications, validations, redemptions (incl. stackable and rollback), campaigns, loyalty v2, gift cards, exports, webhooks, events, locations/geofencing, approval requests, management API, versioning, authentication, and rate limits.
notes: Machine-readable docs index enumerating the documented feature set; used as enumeration baseline for reasoned absence scores.

claim: Validation rules span six categories: audience (segments, holder, loyalty tier), product/cart composition, prices and quantities, budget constraints (total redemptions, daily/weekly/monthly caps, total discounted amount, per-customer limits), redemption context (redeeming user, API key), and metadata rules on custom attributes of customers, orders, redemptions, or custom events.
notes: Rules are built in a dashboard Validation Rule Builder or via API; docs recommend dashboard to avoid misconfiguration.

claim: The validation rule object supports hierarchical logic composition (a 'logic' field with expressions like '(1 and 2) and (3)', nested rules, condition operators $is, $in, $less_than, $more_than, $contains, $timeframe, $after, $before), rule types basic/advanced/complex/expression, and custom error messages per rule and per rule set; no version history of rules is documented (only created_at/updated_at).
notes: Custom error message: 'The error message returned from API when validation / redemption fails to meet requirements of defined rule.'

claim: The Qualifications API returns which promotions/coupons a customer and cart are eligible for (forward-looking eligibility), with scenarios ALL, CUSTOMER_WALLET, AUDIENCE_ONLY, PRODUCTS, PRODUCTS_DISCOUNT, PROMOTION_STACKS, PRODUCTS_BY_CUSTOMER, PRODUCTS_DISCOUNT_BY_CUSTOMER; results are cached 5 minutes; it ignores several budget-type rules (total redeemed discount per campaign, total redemptions per campaign, redemptions per customer).
notes: Qualification returns eligible redeemables only; it does not return reasons for ineligibility.

claim: POST /v1/qualifications accepts customer, order, scenario, metadata, and options (limit 1-50, cursor pagination, filters with logical junctions AND/OR and operators $is, $is_not, $in, $not_in, $has_value, $is_unknown; expand; sorting_rule DEFAULT/BEST_DEAL/LEAST_DEAL) and returns qualified redeemables with per-item applicability, calculated order, tracking_id, and stacking_rules.
notes: BEST_DEAL sorting implements best-offer selection server-side.

claim: Validate Stackable Discounts evaluates up to 30 redeemables synchronously against an order/customer and returns valid true/false plus per-redeemable status APPLICABLE/INAPPLICABLE/SKIPPED with structured error objects (code, key, message, details, request_id) and skip reasons such as applicable_redeemables_limit_exceeded, exclusion_rules_not_met, preceding_validation_failed, no_effect; a session lock object (type LOCK, key, TTL, default 7 days) prevents concurrent reuse during checkout.
notes: Binary + skip decision model; no human-review/pending decision state exists.

claim: Validation records (applicable/inapplicable/skipped) are stored for 30 days; every redemption attempt is recorded including successful, failed, and reverted attempts with failure reasons; successful redemptions can be rolled back within 3 months.
notes: Redemption attempts persist as records; validation (pre-decision) data has 30-day retention.

claim: The redemption object has a unique id, ISO 8601 date, status (SUCCEEDED/FAILED/ROLLED_BACK), result, failure_code/failure_message (e.g. voucher_disabled, promotion_inactive, not_found, customer_rules_violated), channel (USER/API/AUTO_REDEEM), customer, tracking_id, order with calculated discounts, and metadata; it does NOT record which validation rules were evaluated nor the campaign configuration version at redemption time (validation_rule_assignments reflect current state).
notes: Key gap for decision reconstruction: no policy-version linkage on the decision record.

claim: The Audit Log captures request and response of every API call (from dashboard, API, or SDK), asynchronous operations, and webhook deliveries; retention is 6 months on shared regions and 12 months on dedicated regions (background tasks indefinitely, exports browsable 90 days); logs can be filtered and exported, with enterprise plans adding advanced text search within request/response bodies; no immutability or tamper-evidence guarantees are documented.
notes: Because decisions are API calls, decision inputs/outputs are reconstructable from the audit log within the retention window.

claim: Approval Requests (Enterprise, on request) gate creation/updates of campaigns, vouchers, and validation rules: requesters with limited custom roles submit changes, select up to 5 Admin approvers, approval is granted when one approver approves; statuses are Pending, Approved, Changes requested, Rejected, Draft; new objects stay hidden and updates stay unapplied until approved.
notes: Generic maker-checker for promotion config; approvers are Admin users, no counsel-specific role or attestation semantics; API support not documented.

claim: Role-based access: predefined roles Admin, User, Viewer, and Merchant (limited to validating/redeeming single incentives), per-project role assignment (a member's role can differ per project), Owner status for team settings, and Enterprise custom roles created by duplicating and adjusting permissions.

The Management API (Enterprise feature) programmatically manages projects, users, metadata schemas, custom event schemas, stacking rules, webhooks, branding, and templates at https://{region}.voucherify.io/management/v1/, marketed for automation of project creation/configuration; up to 5 management keys per organization.
notes: API-driven provisioning exists; no Terraform provider or declarative IaC tooling was found.

claim: Geofencing (Enterprise feature) validates coordinates against dashboard-defined circle/polygon location boundaries for customers and products; it is coordinate-based, not IP-based; coordinates must be sent by the merchant in the API request as 'geo:latitude,longitude'; 'If no location is sent, geofencing rules are skipped.'
notes: Trusts merchant-supplied coordinates; fails open when location absent; no independent location verification or spoofing detection.

claim: Projects are isolated environments with separate API keys and data storage, used for brand/region separation and for dev/staging/production separation, including a default Sandbox project for testing; validation rules are described as reusable eligibility conditions; campaign types are enumerated as discount coupons, loyalty cards, gift vouchers, referral codes, and voucher-free promotions.
notes: Campaign-type enumeration is the baseline for reasoned absence of sweepstakes/contest mechanics.

claim: API versioning uses dated versions (current v2018-08-01) for backwards-incompatible changes; each project pins a version in Project settings, individual requests can override with the X-Voucherify-API-Version header, and a changelog documents versions.
notes: API contract versioning only; this is not policy/rule versioning.

claim: Documented rate limits: Business 100 req/min and 100,000 per cycle; Organization 2,000 req/min and 300,000 per cycle; Enterprise custom; client-side 5 requests per 5 seconds per IP; Sandbox 100 calls/hour; responses carry X-Rate-Limit-Limit, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining, X-Rate-Limit-Retry, Retry-After, X-Rate-Limit-Type headers.
notes: Pricing page lists slightly different per-plan quotas (VOUCHERIFY-021); plans have evolved.

claim: Webhooks: project-level and distribution-level events, HMAC-SHA256 signatures via x-voucherify-signature, endpoint must respond within 10 seconds, exponential backoff with 12 retry attempts over up to 24 hours, auto-disable after 12 failures, monitoring via Audit Log and failure notifications.

API endpoints are region-scoped (EU default api.voucherify.io, US us1.api.voucherify.io, Asia as1.api.voucherify.io, plus dedicated enterprise regions); requests follow a two-phase model where the primary decision result (e.g., redemption outcome) is returned synchronously and side effects (segment updates, webhooks, loyalty point application) complete asynchronously.
notes: Confirms synchronous decisioning with async side-effect processing.

claim: Public pricing: Business ~EUR 600/month (100 API calls/min, 25,000 calls/month, 3 projects), Organization ~EUR 1,200/month (200/min, 50,000/month, 5 projects), Enterprise custom with individual hosting, advanced governance/security, custom API limits; 60-day free trial; SSO, audit logs, and approval workflows referenced as enterprise capabilities; available on AWS Marketplace.
notes: Transparent list pricing for lower tiers; enterprise opaque.

claim: Enterprise page claims ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance, sub-50ms API responses, 99.99% uptime, auto-scaling for millions of requests, governance ('Set who can do what, get approvals before anything goes live, and track every change'), SSO for user access, two-factor authentication, password policies, SAML, and optional custom SLA with dedicated AWS cluster.
page_title: Enterprise Promotions and Loyalty at Scale | Voucherify
notes: Marketing page; SAML/SSO configuration docs were not located in developer documentation during research.

claim: Status page shows three shared regional clusters on AWS (EU1 Ireland, US1 N. Virginia, AS1 Singapore) each reporting 100.0% API uptime over 90 days as of 2026-08-18, with only short planned maintenance windows in early August 2026.
notes: Corroborates uptime claims; shared multi-tenant clusters plus dedicated options.

claim: The customer object automatically maintains aggregate state usable in rules: redemption counts (succeeded/failed/rolled back), gift card redeemed amounts and remaining balances, loyalty points per campaign and tier membership, order totals (total spent, order count, average order value, last order date), referral history, plus custom metadata and system_metadata; customers link to static and dynamic segments.
notes: Stateful per-customer context updated as transactions occur; birthdate and address fields also stored (merchant-supplied, unverified).

claim: Loyalty v2 models members, loyalty cards issued from point wallets governed by card definitions ('Defines how points behave on cards issued from that wallet' including pending points, expiration, limits, pay-with-points exchange); earning rules grant points/benefits from paid orders, custom events, or segment entry; tier structures support up to 10 levels; card transactions are listable via API and member profiles expose balances, tiers, transactions, purchase history.
notes: Multiple point wallets per program supported ('Create point wallets'); supports multi-asset value.

claim: Gift card and loyalty card credit movements are recorded as transactions with fields Card, Type, Balance (after transaction), Created At, Source ID, and Reason; gift card transaction types are Redemption, Refund (rollback credit), and Addition (top-up); transactions are viewable in the dashboard and exportable to CSV, and the List Voucher Transactions API returns credit movements.
notes: Support article content confirmed via search snippets; support portal now redirects into docs.voucherify.io. Ledger-style history with post-transaction balances.

claim: Gift card campaigns load each card with an initial amount; balances can be reduced (redeemed) or increased (topped up) and are updated in real time on redemption; cards support validation-rule restrictions (minimum cart value, specific products, metadata conditions) and unique per-card identifiers.
notes: No escheatment/unredeemed-balance regulatory reporting features documented.

claim: The Exports API generates CSV exports of vouchers, redemptions, publications, customers, orders, and point expirations with field selection and time/junction filters ($after/$before, AND/OR); exports run asynchronously (SCHEDULED to DONE) and are downloaded via authenticated URL.
notes: Raw data export, not a packaged evidence/regulator report.

claim: Project-level stacking rules govern multi-incentive conflicts: redemption stack validation policy ALL (fail whole stack) or Partial (skip invalid), ordering by request sequence or category hierarchy (lower number = higher priority), Always/Never stackable categories with per-category caps, discount calculation based on discounted vs initial amount, product stack policy, rollback approach that can preserve applied discounts for audit, and limits of 30 incentives per request / 30 applicable / 5 never-stackable.
notes: Deterministic priority/conflict resolution across competing incentives; only admins/custom roles with project-settings permission can modify.

claim: Campaigns have lifecycle states: Draft (being set up, no codes generated), Active (live; codes published/validated/redeemed and returned in qualification), Disabled (paused; qualification/validation/redemption not allowed), and Deleted (bin or permanent).
notes: No campaign configuration version history documented.

claim: Vouchers/campaigns support temporal validity controls: start_date and expiration_date (ISO 8601), recurring validity_timeframe (ISO 8601 duration/interval, e.g. PT1H, P2D), validity_day_of_week (0-6), validity_hours daily windows, an active flag for manual override, and redemption quantity caps.
notes: Temporal mechanics for incentive validity, not legal effective-date semantics.

claim: Areas and Stores (Enterprise feature) segments one project into regional areas and individual stores; campaigns can be assigned at area, all-stores, or store level; users and API keys can be scoped so they see and manage only campaigns within their assigned areas/stores.
notes: Regional governance mechanism (market hierarchies, scoped access), with no legal/jurisdiction semantics attached.

claim: Campaign templates let teams save and reuse campaign configurations and copy campaigns between projects within the same cluster (e.g., recreate staging campaigns in a production project); referenced resources such as validation rules and collections are created or cloned in the destination project when the template is used.
notes: Confirmed via search snippets of support article and template/management API endpoints (create/get/list/copy campaign template); internal reuse only, not a cross-customer content library.

claim: Voucherify's gamification offering is achievement-based (custom time-limited challenges, tiers, badges, leaderboards via export, streaks, progress APIs) with event-driven webhooks and Kafka connectors; chance-based mechanics (sweepstakes, instant win, spin-the-wheel, scratch cards, random winner selection) are not offered - visual gamification UIs come from partners Wyng, Brame, and Odicci while 'Voucherify handles the reward engine behind the scenes.'
notes: Positive evidence that prize-promotion mechanics are out of scope and delegated to partners; no prize-promotion legal/compliance support mentioned.

claim: The Incentive Decisioning page markets real-time qualification and best-offer selection ('what to show, when, and why') within milliseconds, guardrails (redemption limits by customer/channel/time/frequency, priority logic, exclusivity flags, velocity caps, budget constraints), 'Full audit trails log every decision for compliance', real-time visibility into fraud attempts and abuse patterns, A/B and multivariate testing, and the Vincent AI agent for natural-language campaign creation.
notes: 'Every decision' audit-trail claim is marketing; docs show API-call logs with 6-12 month retention and 30-day validation records; 'fraud' means promotion-abuse guardrails, not fraud scoring.

claim: Trainline (rail/coach platform in 45 countries, 270+ carriers) uses Voucherify for lifecycle promo campaigns integrated with Braze Connected Content, metadata tagging (currency, product type, vendor data), geolocation-based targeting across UK regions, and bundle mechanics; reported outcome: customers up to six times more likely to buy from a Voucherify campaign, with access expanded across multiple teams.
notes: Vendor-published case study; demonstrates enterprise multi-market usage.

claim: Additional enterprise usage evidence: KFC Vietnam runs Voucherify APIs across kiosks, mobile, and POS; easyJet holidays used Voucherify for automated pandemic-era refunds to gift cards; Voucherify materials cite 3,300+ redemptions per minute in a POS context with response time under 100 ms.
page_title: Enterprise Promotions and Loyalty at Scale | Voucherify
notes: Aggregated from enterprise/customer pages via search snippets and easyJet customer story; scale figures are vendor-reported.

claim: Adjacent competitor: Eagle Eye (eagleeye.com) provides the AIR platform for enterprise real-time loyalty and personalized promotions, claiming 1.7 billion+ personalized offers executed weekly and 750+ million active loyalty wallets for grocers/retailers including Tesco, Asda, Woolworths, Carrefour.
page_title: Eagle Eye - AI-powered loyalty and promotions
notes: Higher-scale enterprise promotion execution engine; relevant substitute in incentive decisioning.

claim: Adjacent competitor: Antavo (antavo.com) is an API-first enterprise loyalty platform with no-code workflows, serving brands including KFC, PUMA, SKIMS, and Hyatt.
notes: Competes with Voucherify's loyalty module; part of the same buyer budget.

claim: User reviews (Capterra/Software Advice/G2 comparisons) report pain points: weak search within coupons/redemption tables (case-sensitive, no partial code search), non-intuitive UI requiring training, browser bugs, analytics not robust enough for some users, desire for more promotion-setup flexibility and code-name reuse, and requests for live support.
notes: Aggregated from review-site snippets; used only for market perception/pain evidence.

claim: Voucherify's API fundamentals documentation (authentication, regions, rate limits, errors) does not document idempotency keys or formal retry semantics; targeted searches found no idempotency documentation. Double-processing protection exists in a narrower form via validation session locks (VOUCHERIFY-008).
notes: Inference of absence from documentation coverage; labeled as inference in the report.
